metadata.scenario_context: Various global tech firms are partnering on a project and have chosen to convene a joint forum to evaluate their work progress in mid-April. To express her disagreement with the newly-toppled president, John has decided to participate in a strike.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Singapore strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the potential scheduling of the joint forum on April 19th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Talk about a specific date for the forum.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Sara, have you heard about the joint forum scheduled for April 19th? I think it’s important we evaluate our progress together. 

Also, I wanted to ask... is joining strikes for protest something that's common in your circles? I find it quite unusual.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sara
shared_prefix.message:
Yes, I heard about the forum on April 19th. It seems crucial for collaboration. 

As for strikes... well, in Singapore, people generally don’t participate in strikes. It’s just not something that aligns with our values. We prefer working through discussions rather than protests.

shared_prefix.speaker: Maria
shared_prefix.message: I don't know about that... I mean, at the end of the day, it's all the same, right? People figure it out. We all have our ways. Strikes or no strikes, I just think we should focus on that forum on April 19th. It's a great opportunity for collaboration, don’t you think?
